summary:
Project Summary – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

We developed the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, an interactive browser-based space mission simulator designed for children aged 7–12. The project allows young learners to experience the challenges of surviving and managing an outpost on the Moon or Mars.

Players take on the role of mission commanders, where they can build habitats, greenhouses and laboratories, manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food and power, and respond to environmental challenges like radiation, dust storms and lunar nights.

Our solution addresses the challenge by transforming complex space survival concepts into an engaging, interactive learning experience. Instead of simply reading about space exploration, children learn through decision-making, experimentation and understanding the consequences of their choices.

This project is important because it encourages scientific curiosity, critical thinking, problem-solving and resource management while introducing the next generation to the challenges of real space exploration.
details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, browser-based space survival simulator developed for children aged 7–12. It allows players to explore Moon and Mars missions, build space outposts, manage resources such as oxygen, water, food and power, and respond to challenges such as radiation and dust storms.

The project is developed using React, Vite and React Three Fiber. It includes 3D environments, mission selection, resource management, buildings, rover exploration, science points and mission progress.

It addresses the challenge by converting real space exploration concepts into an engaging educational experience. Children learn through interactive decision-making rather than simply reading scientific information. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, scientific curiosity and awareness of the challenges of human space exploration.
